data.long_meaning: Bryan derives from the Old Norse name Briani, meaning ‘strong, powerful, honorable.’ In Irish mythology, Brian was a high king of Munster, and in Christian tradition, St. Bryan was a bishop in Armorica. in_latin.name: Bryan

in_english.name: Bryan
in_english.long_meaning: The name Bryan originates from the Celtic word 'brig', meaning 'noble' or 'high', and 'an', meaning 'son'. Hence, Bryan signifies 'son of the noble one' or 'strong, honorable man'. Although not directly mentioned in the Bible, similar names convey notions of nobility, spiritual strength, and dignity. Historically, Bryan has been used in Christian traditions to denote respect and virtue.

data.cultural_impact: The name Bryan has been popular in both the English-speaking world and Ireland throughout history, with many notable figures and cultural references. In Ireland, Bryan Ferry—an English musician—has Celtic roots and there is a town named Bryanstown in County Kerry. These associations reflect the importance and influence of the name throughout history and culture.
